newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian shares sluggish, market index dips.
newsitem.headline: Estonian shares sluggish, market index dips.

text.p: Shares on the Estonian stock exchange were sluggish on Tuesday with both the official and the over-the-counter free market list turning over just more than six million kroons and the market index dipping.
Official list trade came in at 6.7 million kroons, slightly lower than the free market volume of 6.9 million kroons. The Tallinn stock exchange index slipped 1.04 percent to 104.25.

Savings Bank was the most active on the main list, with turnover of 3.3 million kroons. It closed sharply lower at 37.60 kroons after 39.35 kroons. Dealers said there was strong selling pressure on the stock.
On the free market, department store Tallinna Kaubamaja was in the spotlight as it forecast improved 1996 earnings and announced it was to open a branch in Helsinki.
It turned over 2.6 million kroons and closed at 58 kroons, versus 57.75 kroons.

"Kaubamaja's September net profit of 3.6 million kroons is a very good result and as the end of the year (Christmas season) is moving closer, the shares are quite attractive," said Savings Bank trader Charlie Viikberg.
Drug company Tallinn Pharmaceutical saw trade of one million kroons and it closed at 55.90 kroons after 53.50 kroons. It earlier said that its nine-month profit was 18 million kroons.
